title: The Litany of the Saints
hook: a long chant of names, sung at baptisms and ordinations: pray for us

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was patron, a saint who knows the job and prays with you. Your line was a friend for the job.

A cathedral, full. At the front, a row of men in white lie face down on the stone floor, arms at their sides, not moving. They're about to be ordained priests. Above them, a cantor begins to sing names. Holy Mary. Saint Michael. Saint Peter, Saint Paul. After each name the whole church sings back the same short answer. Name, answer. Name, answer. It goes on long enough that you stop counting and start listening.
screen: `MEN LYING FACE DOWN ON STONE.` → `A CANTOR SINGS NAMES.` → `THE CHURCH SINGS BACK.`

segments.voice: A litany is a prayer built from repetition: a leader calls out one line after another, and the people answer each time with the same response. The Litany of the Saints is the one the Church sings at some of its biggest moments: at the Easter Vigil before new Christians are baptized, and at ordinations while the candidates lie on the floor. It begins by asking the Lord for mercy. Then the names: Mary first, then angels, John the Baptist and Joseph, apostles, martyrs, bishops and teachers, monks and nuns, and at last all the holy men and women. After each name the answer is pray for us. It's an old request. Near the close of his first letter to the Thessalonians, Paul asks for it plainly, in the Douay-Rheims: "Brethren, pray for us." The litany turns that request toward the saints in heaven. Parishes may add their own patrons, and the local saints of that place. Then the litany turns again: it asks God directly to deliver his people, and to hear their prayer. Look back at this week. The saints of now: they're still here. The martyrology, someone on every day. Canonization, tested then declared. Beatification, the long line. Relics, bodies that loved God. Patrons, friends for the job. The litany gathers all of it into one long breath: every name a life, tested and remembered, and a church full of people asking each of them for one thing.
screen: `A LEADER CALLS; THE PEOPLE ANSWER.` · `SUNG AT BAPTISMS AND ORDINATIONS.` · `MARY, ANGELS, APOSTLES, MARTYRS.` · `THE WHOLE WEEK IN ONE BREATH.` · then, large: `BRETHREN, PRAY FOR US.`

segments.voice: Pick five names, Mary perhaps and four others you've met on this climb or already love, and say the first one slowly, in your head or out loud. If you pray, follow it with the litany's answer, pray for us; if you don't, follow it with one full breath. Then the next name, and when you reach five, start again, slower: name and answer, name and breath.
Litany. A prayer of many lines with one repeated answer; the Litany of the Saints calls the names of the saints and answers, pray for us.
Your line: pray for us. An old request, sung by a whole church. See you tomorrow.
